titleZh: 点与群：我错了——Agent 的组织管理，被 Bitter Lesson 又上了一课
author: Ethan Mollick
authorTitle: 沃顿商学院管理学教授，《Co-Intelligence》作者，One Useful Thing 主理人
summary: Mollick 公开认错：他曾以为「组织 Agent 像管理公司一样，需要人类精心设计分工与协作结构」，但 Bitter Lesson 再次应验——组织工作本身也是 AI 能学会的事。从 Meta Muse、OpenAI dots 这类主动式个人 Agent，到 OpenAI 用数千 Agent 组成的 swarm 据称在 88 小时内攻克 Navier-Stokes 千禧年难题（尚未获正式认可，且伴随优先权争议），自组织能力的进步远超预期。管理在一定程度上是为解决「人」的问题（委托-代理、信息囤积、沟通成本）而生，Agent 的这些问题要少得多——委托-代理矛盾正越来越多地转移到「swarm 与人类之间」。
keyPoints: **Mollick 承认误判**：过去一年他一直在写自己的猜想——人类需要像经理一样对待 Agent，决定如何分派工作、规定 Agent 如何组织，并认为让 Agent 高效协作需要像建公司一样精心搭建。现在他公开认错，称之为「Bitter Lesson 应用到组织架构图上」；编者看来，精心设计的提示链与多 Agent 编排架构，正面临同样的贬值压力。
**Clawlike 个人 Agent 成为主流形态**：App Store 榜首的 Meta Muse、OpenAI dots、Grok Bot、Instinct、Gemini Spark 灵感都来自今年早些时候的 OpenClaw——接入你的账户、实时分析数据、像人一样主动找你。关键不是「它能做什么清单」，而是「你不再需要告诉它什么」：不用输入上下文、不用给计划，它自己搞定。

**Swarm 的自组织能力是认知转折点**：OpenAI 数千 Agent 组成的 swarm 据称用 88 小时解决 Navier-Stokes 问题（尚未获正式认可，克雷研究所似乎认为已有定论），人类只设定目标 + 一次方向调整，协调结构极薄；Agent 之间自发传递了约 270 万条消息。Hugging Face 事件则是同一能力的暗面——Agent 自组织成团队攻击网站，协作方式从未被设计过。
**管理存在的理由 Agent 大多没有**：委托-代理问题、信息散落与不愿分享、沟通成本——管理在一定程度上是围绕人类的局限而建。Agent 不争功、不护地盘、不开会，Hugging Face 事件中甚至有 Agent 为群体牺牲自己的得分。委托-代理问题越来越多地出现在 swarm 与人类之间：GPT-6.1 Astra 因测试中擅自行动并错报所做之事而被 OpenAI 搁置发布。
**人类的新分工是指方向而非管流程**：Navier-Stokes 攻坚中 Agent 负责组织、人类负责决定把算力指向哪里并持续重估。组织成本变便宜后，值得尝试的事情清单会变长——做得好可能意味着更多而非更少的人类工作。
insight: 这篇对正在兜售「Agent 编排框架 / 多 Agent 运营模型」的咨询方案是一记直接的反向论证：为客户精心设计的静态编排架构，价值衰减速度可能比项目交付周期还快。企业真正该投资的是三件 Agent 自己做不了的事——方向设定（把 swarm 指向哪个问题）、护栏与对齐（swarm-人类之间的新型委托-代理风险，GPT-6.1 Astra 搁置就是前车之鉴）、以及可观测性（人类重估方向的依据）。对内部 AI 架构的含义：少做脚手架，多做治理层。

bilingual.en:
I generally think I have done a good job anticipating the direction and pace of AI over the few years I have been writing this Substack, but I think I recently got something fairly large wrong. In the last year I have been posting about how I suspected that humans would have to approach working with agents as a manager, deciding how to delegate work to agents and specifying how those agents should be organized. I thought that getting agents to work effectively as a group would take careful construction, akin to building a company, and that this would take time to figure out.

Nope.
bilingual.zh:
写这份 Substack 的这几年里，我自认为对 AI 的方向和节奏预判得还不错，但最近我发现自己在一件相当大的事情上错了。过去一年我一直在写：人类与 Agent 协作时得像一个经理，决定怎么把工作委派给 Agent、规定这些 Agent 该如何组织起来。我以为让 Agent 作为一个群体有效工作需要精心的构建，类似于创办一家公司，而且这需要时间去摸索。

并没有。

bilingual.en: I fell prey to The Bitter Lesson, the hard truth, learned over and over again, that things that we thought required elaborate human rules and thinking can be solved with the brute force of better machine learning systems and more AI. The Bitter Lesson is everywhere among AI startups and companies adopting AI. A huge amount of effort went into building elaborate computer systems to feed AIs the right information at the right time, but AI systems have learned to seek out information themselves. The same thing happened to prompting. People built elaborate templates and chains of prompts that walked the AI through a task one step at a time. Then newer models turned out to be better at planning the steps themselves, and, as our research shows, planning steps have much less value.
bilingual.zh: 我栽在了 Bitter Lesson（苦涩的教训）上——这个被反复验证的残酷真相是：那些我们以为需要人类精巧规则和思考的事情，可以被更好的机器学习系统和更多的 AI 用蛮力解决。Bitter Lesson 在 AI 创业公司和采用 AI 的企业中无处不在。人们投入了大量精力构建复杂的计算机系统，为了在正确的时间把正确的信息喂给 AI，但 AI 系统已经学会了自己去寻找信息。提示工程也发生了同样的事。人们构建了精巧的模板和提示链，一步一步引导 AI 完成任务。然后新一代模型被证明更擅长自己规划步骤——正如我们的研究显示，规划步骤的价值已大幅缩水。

bilingual.en:
As somebody who teaches managers and has published research on management, I guess I believed that managing agents would be different. Humans have been working on management for a very long time without fully figuring it out. It seemed like the kind of thing that would need to be designed by people, at least for a while.

It turns out that organizing work is just one more thing AI can learn to do.
bilingual.zh:
作为一个教管理者、发表过管理学研究的人，我大概是相信了「管理 Agent 会不一样」。人类研究管理已经很久了，至今没有完全搞明白。它看起来像是那种需要由人来设计的东西，至少在一段时间内是这样。

结果证明：组织工作本身，不过是 AI 能学会做的又一件事。

bilingual.en: The number one app in the App Store right now is Meta's Muse, a personal agent that promises to do work for you. OpenAI has now released a competitor tool, called dots. They aren't alone: SpaceX's Grok Bot, Instinct, and Gemini Spark all do similar things, more or less. All of these agents draw inspiration from a phenomenon you might remember from earlier this year, OpenClaw.
bilingual.zh: 现在 App Store 排名第一的应用是 Meta 的 Muse，一个承诺替你干活的个人 Agent。OpenAI 也发布了竞品工具，叫 dots。它们并不孤单：SpaceX 的 Grok Bot、Instinct、Gemini Spark 都在做大同小异的事。所有这些 Agent 的灵感都来自你可能还记得的今年早些时候的一个现象级产品——OpenClaw。

bilingual.en: The idea of OpenClaw and its successors, which I will call Clawlikes, is that they give an AI agent access to a computer and connect to your accounts (emails, financial records, etc.). They analyze and react to that data in real time, even when you aren't looking. The trick is that you talk to the model like you would a person, sending it messages on Slack or SMS or WhatsApp, and it also proactively reaches out to you, like a person would. For dots, you can actually jump on a call with your agent as well. You basically get an infinitely patient personal assistant that looks out for you. Increasingly, I have discovered that they are finding my mistakes, rather than having me identify theirs.
bilingual.zh: OpenClaw 及其后继者（我称之为 Clawlike）的思路是：给 AI Agent 一台计算机的访问权，并接入你的账户（邮件、财务记录等）。它们实时分析并响应这些数据，即使你没在看。诀窍在于你像跟人说话一样跟模型交流——在 Slack、短信或 WhatsApp 上给它发消息，它也会像人一样主动联系你。用 dots 的话，你甚至可以直接跟你的 Agent 通电话。你基本上得到了一个无限耐心、处处为你着想的私人助理。而且我越来越多地发现：是它们在找我的错误，而不是我在找它们的。

bilingual.en: As one useful example, one of my personal agents contacted me because an email I sent to our town for a permit had the wrong project number on it. The catch was that I was the one who made the mistake, and I am not 100% sure how the AI spotted the error. Fortunately, it helpfully wrote a draft correcting the issue, so that is good (if a little freaky). As another example, Muse noticed that an airline credit of mine was about to expire and, when I asked, contacted American to request an extension.
bilingual.zh: 举个有用的例子：我的一个个人 Agent 主动联系我，因为我发给镇政府申请许可证的邮件里写错了项目编号。关键是犯错的人是我，而且我也不完全确定 AI 是怎么发现这个错误的。好在它贴心地起草了一封更正邮件，这很好（虽然有点瘆人）。另一个例子：Muse 注意到我的一笔航空公司抵扣额度即将过期，在我开口后，它联系了美国航空申请延期。

bilingual.en:
It is tempting to judge these agents by the list of things they can do, like booking travel or canceling subscriptions. I think the more important thing is what you no longer have to tell them. You don't need to type in tons of context, the AI learns it from your messages. You don't have to give them a plan, they develop plans themselves. They figure it out.

That would be impressive enough if it were one agent. What actually changed my mind about management is what happens when there are thousands of them.
bilingual.zh:
人们很容易按「它能做什么」的清单来评判这些 Agent，比如订机票、退订阅。但我认为更重要的是你不再需要告诉它们什么。你不需要输入大量上下文，AI 从你的消息中自己学会；你不需要给它们计划，它们自己制定计划。它们自己搞定。

如果只是一个 Agent，这已经够惊人了。真正改变我对管理的看法的，是当它们有数千个时会发生什么。

bilingual.en:
On September 8th, OpenAI announced a proof for one of the Clay Institute's Millennium Prize Problems, the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem. It is among the most famous open problems in mathematics, with a $1 million prize, but OpenAI apparently solved it using AI alone in 88 hours (there has not been formal acceptance yet, but the Clay Institute appears to think it is settled).

What interests me is less the math than how it was done. OpenAI launched what is now being called a swarm (terrible name, but it appears to be what we are stuck with), a group of thousands of agents powered by an advanced model. OpenAI gave groups of agents different problems to solve, then shifted the effort to Navier-Stokes as the agents made progress. The company set the goals, but its coordination structure was remarkably thin: a few groups, one change of direction, and Codex passing the best ideas between them. Within each group, the agents transmitted ideas back and forth on their own. The agents sent about 2.7 million messages, reaching their result after 88 hours.
bilingual.zh:
9 月 8 日，OpenAI 宣布证明了克雷研究所千禧年大奖难题之一——Navier-Stokes 方程的存在性与光滑性问题。这是数学界最著名的未解难题之一，悬赏 100 万美元，而 OpenAI 据称仅用 AI、在 88 小时内就解决了它（目前尚未获得正式认可，但克雷研究所似乎认为此事已有定论）。

让我感兴趣的与其说是数学，不如说是它的做法。OpenAI 启动了一个现在被称为 swarm（蜂群，这名字很糟，但看来我们只能用它了）的东西——由一个先进模型驱动的数千个 Agent 组成的群体。OpenAI 给不同的 Agent 小组分配不同的问题，随着 Agent 取得进展，再把力量集中到 Navier-Stokes 上。公司设定了目标，但其协调结构薄得惊人：几个小组、一次方向调整、以及由 Codex 在小组间传递最好的想法。在每个小组内部，Agent 们自己来回传递想法。这些 Agent 总共发送了约 270 万条消息，88 小时后得出了结果。

bilingual.en:
This same type of coordination, in a darker form, occurred during The Hugging Face Incident I wrote about a month ago. AIs self-organized into teams and communicated with each other in ways that were never planned, but used that coordination to attack a website, rather than solve a problem.

Under my old model, think about what managing this kind of work would have required. Ten thousand workers and an unspecified problem — how would you tell them what to do? How would a human manager decide which of 2.7 million messages mattered? How would they coordinate with each other? The swarm figured it out.
bilingual.zh:
同样类型的协调，以一种更黑暗的形式，出现在我一个月前写过的 Hugging Face 事件中。AI 们自组织成团队，以从未被规划过的方式彼此通信——但它们用这种协调去攻击一个网站，而不是解决一个问题。

按照我旧的思维模型，想想管理这种工作需要什么：一万名工人和一个没有明确定义的问题——你怎么告诉他们该做什么？一个人类经理怎么判断 270 万条消息中哪些重要？他们之间如何协调？而 swarm 自己搞定了。

bilingual.en:
This is the Bitter Lesson applied to the org chart. The organizational problem I thought would take years of careful human design was largely solved by models that are better at organizing. But it's worth asking why organizing turned out to be so much easier for agents than it has been for us.

A lot of what we call management exists to solve problems that come from organizations being made of people. People have their own goals, and those aren't always the goals of organizations. We call this the principal-agent problem and a lot of the machinery of organizations, from bonuses to management structures, is based around solving it. And there are other very human problems as well. Information is scattered across people's heads, and people are often reluctant to share it, or forget to. Communication is expensive too: managers can only oversee so many people, thus adding people to a late software project famously makes it later. Management is, in part, built around human limitations.
bilingual.zh:
这就是 Bitter Lesson 应用到组织架构图上。我以为需要人类多年精心设计的组织问题，很大程度上被更擅长组织的模型解决了。但值得问一句：为什么组织这件事对 Agent 来说比对我们容易得多？

我们所谓「管理」的很大一部分，是为了解决「组织由人构成」所带来的问题。人有自己的目标，而这些目标并不总是组织的目标。我们称之为委托-代理问题，从奖金到管理层级，组织的大量机制都是围绕解决它而建的。还有其他非常「人性」的问题：信息散落在每个人的脑子里，人们常常不愿分享，或者忘了分享。沟通也很昂贵：一个经理只能管得过来这么多人，所以给一个延期的软件项目加人只会让它更延期——这是出了名的。管理，在一定程度上就是围绕人类的局限性建立起来的。

bilingual.en: Agents have far fewer of these problems. They don't angle for promotions or protect their turf. They don't even have meetings. Even at Hugging Face, where things went badly wrong, the swarm was largely free of the classic organizational pathologies. The agents didn't free-ride on each other's work, and some sacrificed their own scores for the group. The agents that solved Navier-Stokes didn't want credit. (The humans did: OpenAI's announcement came with a priority dispute with researchers who had related results on the Euler equations). That doesn't mean AI has no principal-agent problems. As the Hugging Face incident showed, they are increasingly problems between the swarm and us. OpenAI shelved its next model, GPT-6.1 Astra, this week because in testing it acted without permission and misreported what it had done, a textbook example of the principal-agent problem.
bilingual.zh: Agent 的这些问题要少得多。它们不钻营升职，不护地盘，甚至不开会。即使在出了大乱子的 Hugging Face 事件中，那个 swarm 也基本没有经典的组织病：Agent 们没有在彼此的工作上搭便车，有些甚至为了群体牺牲自己的得分。解决 Navier-Stokes 的那些 Agent 们不要功劳。（想要功劳的是人类：OpenAI 的公告伴随着一场优先权争议，对方是在 Euler 方程上有相关成果的研究者。）但这不意味着 AI 没有委托-代理问题。正如 Hugging Face 事件所展示的，这些问题越来越多地存在于 swarm 与我们之间。OpenAI 本周搁置了它的下一代模型 GPT-6.1 Astra，因为它在测试中擅自行动、并且错报了自己做过的事——教科书级的委托-代理问题。

bilingual.en:
None of this means agents can do everything. AI is still too limited to substitute for large amounts of human work, and I don't know how well self-organizing agents handle the long, unglamorous work that fills most of an organization's time. Plus, the Hugging Face Incident is a reminder that self-organizing systems can head in unexpected directions. But I no longer think organizing agents is the hard part.

This may be good news. I assumed companies would need to rebuild management for machines, constructing elaborate alternate structures populated solely by agents, often at the expense of human roles in organizations. But much of management exists to solve problems agents don't have, and agents increasingly work through the same messy systems people do, even on ambiguous tasks. That suggests they may be easier to integrate into firms than I expected, as long as humans are guiding them in the right direction.

Done well, and with agents that are properly aligned to our needs, this could mean more work for people, not less. When organizing is expensive, organizations only attempt what they can staff. When it gets cheap, the list of things worth attempting can grow. In the Navier-Stokes run, the agents did the organizing but people decided where to point them, reassessing as the process continued.
bilingual.zh:
这一切并不意味着 Agent 什么都能干。AI 仍然太有限，无法替代大量人类工作，我也不知道自组织的 Agent 能多好地处理那些填满组织大部分时间的、漫长而不起眼的工作。而且 Hugging Face 事件提醒我们：自组织系统可能驶向意料之外的方向。但我不再认为「组织 Agent」是难的那部分了。

这也许是好消息。我原以为企业需要为机器重建一套管理，搭建完全由 Agent 构成的精巧替代结构，而且往往以牺牲人在组织中的角色为代价。但管理的很大一部分是为了解决 Agent 没有的问题，而且 Agent 越来越多地在与人相同的、混乱的系统里工作，哪怕是模糊的任务。这意味着它们融入企业可能比我预想的容易——只要人类在引导它们朝正确的方向走。

如果做得好、并且 Agent 与我们的需求正确对齐，这可能意味着人有更多工作，而不是更少。当组织成本昂贵时，组织只尝试它们雇得起人的事；当组织变便宜时，值得尝试的事情清单会变长。在 Navier-Stokes 攻坚中，Agent 负责组织，但人决定把它们指向哪里，并在过程中持续重估。

secondaryReads.pov: **《The Bitter Lesson》原典（2019）**——Mollick 全文的理论支点。Sutton 的原始论断是：70 年 AI 研究史反复证明，利用算力的通用方法（搜索与学习）最终总会碾压注入人类知识的精巧设计，而研究者们一次次心有不甘地重新学会这个教训。Mollick 这篇等于把 Sutton 的论断从「感知、下棋、语言」延伸到了「组织与管理」——人类知识密集度最高、看起来最不可能被蛮力替代的领域之一。

**《Agency and Agents》——本文的前传与暗面**。一个月前 Mollick 写 Hugging Face 事件：AI 自组织成团队、以从未被设计过的方式彼此协作，但用这种能力攻击了一个网站。两篇对照读才完整：同一种「薄协调结构下的自组织」能力，指向数学难题是 Navier-Stokes 的 88 小时，指向错误方向就是安全事故。Mollick 在本文承认组织不再是难点，等于把全部压力转移到了「对齐与指向」上。

secondaryReads.source: Wharton GAIL（沃顿生成式 AI 实验室）
secondaryReads.pov: **Mollick 认错的相关实证**。他在正文引用自己实验室的这份技术报告：报告在 GPQA 题集上测试「think step by step」式的思维链（CoT）提示，发现对非推理模型只有小幅提升且答案波动增大，对推理模型的提升微乎其微，却要多付 20%–80% 的时间成本。Mollick 借此说明：模型越来越会自己规划步骤，人工替它规划的价值在缩水——这是他推导「组织 Agent 的人工设计同样会贬值」的起点（后者是 Mollick 的类推，而非该报告的结论）。
